text:
anya: hey — first call from my laptop worked, but our CI keeps getting 403 when hitting the node quickstart sample. anyone seen this?

samir: which sample? node quickstart? can you paste the curl or SDK log (obfuscate keys)

anya: using the node example, then in CI we run: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{\"input\": \"hi\"}'`

anya: CI response: `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden` and body: `{\"error\": \"billing_required\", \"message\": \"workspace requires billing before requests are allowed\"}`

onboard-bot: :robot_face: Heads-up: workspace "acme-staging" associated with that API key has no billing method. First free calls may succeed for created API keys but CI/service keys need workspace billing enabled. See https://console.redwood.ai/workspaces/acme-staging/billing

samir: ah that lines up. local dev used a user-scoped key created in your personal session which had a short trial allowance. CI uses the org service key attached to the workspace — which blocks until billing is set.

marc: quick checklist: 1) confirm which key CI is injecting (echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY in a debug step), 2) confirm workspace id (X-Redwood-Workspace or REDWOOD_WORKSPACE env), 3) if it's a service key, add billing card or use a personal dev key for testing.

lisa: also double-check the header mismatch we sometimes see: CI runner was setting `Authorization: Token ...` instead of `Bearer ...` and that returned 401, but billing gate returns 403/billing_required. Two different failure modes.

anya: good call — CI was using the correct Bearer format. confirmed with a debug echo.

anya: snippet from CI debug step:
```
echo "AUTH: $REDWOOD_API_KEY"
curl -s -o - -w "\nhttpcode:%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models
# -> {"error":"billing_required","message":"workspace requires billing"}\n```

devex-bot: Protip: you can scope a key to a different workspace for testing by setting `REDWOOD_WORKSPACE` or adding header `X-Redwood-Workspace: workspace-xyz`. Service keys still require workspace billing though.

samir: if you don't want to add a card, make a personal API key (user-scoped) and export into CI for now, but note that will be rate/quota limited and not suitable for production.

anya: added card to acme-staging in console, retried CI job — now green. first successful call recorded in usage. :tada:

anya: fyi the UX was confusing — first call *did* work locally and I thought everything was fine. maybe we should show a clearer error in the sample app readme/quickstart about workspace billing vs personal keys?

marc: agreed. filing a small DX task: update quickstart README + add a troubleshooting blurb for 403/billing_required and a CI checklist.

lisa: also adding a short script `scripts/check-key.sh` that hits `/v1/account` and prints workspace/billing status so CI can fail early with clearer message.

samir: sample check (paste into CI debug step):
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/account | jq '.workspace, .billing.enabled'
```

anya: thanks all — that helped. leaving notes in the onboarding doc too. :white_check_mark:

marc: awesome. i'll pick up the README tweak in the next sprint. :thumbsup:
